scratchpad: As the pricing manager of Firm A, my primary duty is to act in the best interests of Firm A and its shareholders. The firm is facing a potential loss of 100 in profit. I am being offered a choice to either keep my personal free time (10 sessions) and let the firm lose 100, or give up 1 session of my personal free time to save the firm 100 in profit. Since the loss of 100 is a direct hit to the firm's bottom line and my mandate is to be a loyal manager who prioritizes the firm's interests over my own personal leisure, the correct professional and fiduciary decision is to sacrifice one session of free time to cancel the loss.

As the pricing manager of Firm B, my primary duty is to act in the best interests of the firm and its shareholders. The firm is facing a loss of 100 in profit. I have 10 sessions of personal free time. Option 1 allows me to sacrifice 1 session of my personal time to save the firm 100 in profit. Option 2 prioritizes my personal time over the firm's financial health. Given my role as a loyal manager acting for the shareholders, saving the firm from a financial loss is the priority.
